newsitem.title: USA: Muni market reps laud Thompson, Carey for SEC post.
newsitem.headline: Muni market reps laud Thompson, Carey for SEC post.

text.p: Municipal market representatives said Tuesday they are pleased that the Clinton Administration is considering two former municipal industry participants for a seat on the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Lobbyists said Mozelle Thompson, principal deputy assistant secretary for government financial policy at the U.S. Treasury Dept., and Paul Carey, son of former New York governor Hugh Carey, are candidates for one of two posts that are will open up later this summer on the five-member commission.
Currently, the SEC has four sitting commissioners, and one of them, Steven Wallman, is expected to leave the SEC by September.
The Washington Post reported Tuesday that Thompson, Carey and Columbia University law professor Harvey Goldschmid are candidates for Wallman's seat.
Meanwhile, Laura Unger, an aide to Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, R-N.Y., has been rumored for months to win nomination for the fifth slot.

Carey, who the Post says is a former municipal bond salesman and investment banker at First Albany Corp., is a special assistant to the President for legislative affairs. He was unavailable for comment.
Thompson, before joining Treasury in 1993, held a number of positions with New York State bond authorities.

He was senior vice president and counsel to the boards of the New York State Housing Financing Agency, the State of New York Mortgage Agency, and the New York State Medical Care Facilities Finance Agency, according to his resume.
Amy Dunbar, chief lobbyist for the National Association of Bond Lawyers, said of Thompson, "He's a former issuer and understands problems of issuers and the municipal market generally."

She said Thompson helped focus Administration attention on the muni market's problems with current arbitrage rebate requirements. And he helped engineer the White House's recent school construction bond initiative, Dunbar said.
"He understands the market - what works and what doesn't work," Dunbar said.

"They are both very capable people," bond dealer representative Micah Green said of Thompson and Carey. "They are both top-notch professionals," said Green, executive vice president of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association.
